units.text: Ruling on ghusl for a wet dream that leaves no trace

Q: Question from Ibrahim. A. H. He says: Sometimes I remember having a wet dream after I wake up, but I do not see any trace of that wet dream. Do I have to perform ghusl or not? Please give us a fatwa, may Allah reward you with good.

A: Ghusl is not obligatory for someone who sees a wet dream unless he finds water, which is semen, because the Prophet ﷺ said: "Water is from water," meaning that the water of ghusl is from the water of semen. This is according to the scholars regarding the one who has a wet dream. However, if he has intercourse with his wife, then he must perform ghusl even if no water comes out, because the Prophet ﷺ said: "When the two circumcised parts meet, ghusl becomes obligatory." Reported by Muslim in his Sahih. And he ﷺ said: "When he sits between her four limbs and then strives with her, ghusl becomes obligatory." Agreed upon its authenticity. Muslim added in his Sahih: "Even if he does not ejaculate."
In the two Sahihs, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, that Umm Sulaym al-Ansariyyah – the mother of Anas, may Allah be pleased with them both – said: O Messenger of Allah, Allah is not shy of the truth. Is ghusl required for a woman if she has a wet dream? The Prophet ﷺ said: "Yes, if she sees water."
This ruling applies to both men and women according to all scholars. And included in this meaning: whoever ejaculates semen due to desire, from thinking or touching, then ghusl is obligatory upon him, like the one who has a wet dream if he ejaculates, because of the general statement of the Prophet ﷺ: "Water is from water." Allah is the Guardian of success.⟦N1⟧
Published in Majallat al-Da'wah, issue (955) on 23/11/1404 AH. And in the book al-Da'wah (al-Fatawa) by His Eminence, part 1, pp. 40-41, (Majmu' Fatawa wa Maqalat al-Shaykh Ibn Baz 10/179).
